question: For the already selected densitized V=0 constraint H_hat with spectral multiplier h(kappa,p)=3*p^2-2*hbar^2*kappa^2, does the standard positive group-average measure on the p>0 zero ray extend across p=0 on a test domain containing amplitudes nonzero at the origin, or does a cutoff expose a logarithmic divergence and subtraction-scale ambiguity that require extra edge data?

upstream_results.role: fixes the selected H_hat spectral multiplier and the interior p>0 measure dp/(2*sqrt(6)*hbar*p) while leaving p=0 completion null

primary_sources.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, 6.2.1 and 6.2.4
primary_sources.used_for: the defining integral E1(z)=integral_z^infinity exp(-t)dt/t and the identity E1(z)=Ein(z)-log(z)-EulerGamma
primary_sources.not_used_for: selecting a cosmological test domain, endpoint counterterm, sector, or physical interpretation

primary_sources.source: Marolf, Refined Algebraic Quantization: Systems with a single constraint, arXiv:gr-qc/9508015
primary_sources.used_for: the single-constraint refined-algebraic-quantization framework and its dependence on auxiliary choices
primary_sources.not_used_for: deriving the repository-specific p=0 cutoff integral or selecting its completion

primary_sources.source: Giulini, Group Averaging and Refined Algebraic Quantization, arXiv:gr-qc/0003040
primary_sources.used_for: the general group-averaging framework and its stated limitations and uniqueness questions
primary_sources.not_used_for: turning this local minisuperspace boundary result into quantum gravity

primary_sources.source: Louko and Martinez-Pascual, Constraint rescaling in refined algebraic quantisation: momentum constraint, arXiv:1107.1092
primary_sources.used_for: the boundary that classically equivalent constraint rescalings may yield quantum equivalence, failure, or self-adjoint-extension ambiguity depending on extra data
primary_sources.not_used_for: claiming that their momentum-constraint examples solve raw C or the p=0 edge in this model

declared_model.upstream_operator: the selected self-adjoint densitized H_hat in Fourier-Kontorovich-Lebedev variables
declared_model.branch: closed first quadrant kappa>=0,p>=0 approached from the established open component kappa>0,p>0
declared_model.cutoff: p>=epsilon with epsilon>0; no delta(uv) identity is asserted at the singular origin
declared_model.subtraction_convention: for a positive reference momentum p_star, inspect FP_pstar=lim_{epsilon->0+}[eta_epsilon[A_0,A_0]-log(p_star/epsilon)/(2*sqrt(6)*hbar)] only as a diagnostic, not as a selected rigging map

assumptions: hbar is strictly positive and numerical witnesses use hbar=1
the upstream Fourier-Kontorovich-Lebedev spectral realization and p>0 coarea measure are not changed
the cutoff calculation agrees with the standard positive p>0 group average before the p=0 limit
a positive rigging form must assign finite norm to every amplitude admitted to its declared test domain
a subtraction scale or an origin-supported sector is extra data and is not selected by the cutoff itself
tasks: derive the x,y and u,v Jacobians and the zero-ray dp/p weight without using the singular delta(uv) identity at u=0
derive eta_epsilon[A_0,A_0]=E1(2*epsilon)/(2*sqrt(6)*hbar) and its universal logarithmic coefficient
show that finite-part values at two positive reference momenta differ by a nonzero logarithm
independently compare direct high-precision quadrature with E1 at three fixed cutoffs and check the finite witness
leave raw C, rescaling equivalence, a canonical p=0 completion, endpoint data, lapse/BFV completion, physics and TOE outputs null

decision_table.condition: the exact shell measure has dp/p, the nonzero-edge witness diverges logarithmically, the vanishing witness is finite, reference-scale finite parts differ, and all independent quadratures pass
the nonzero-edge witness has a finite cutoff-independent positive norm with no extra choice
any Jacobian, shell weight, E1, logarithmic coefficient, finite witness, scale-shift, or independent quadrature check fails

computed_scope: one exact change of variables for the selected spectral multiplier
one positive on-shell cutoff form for p>=epsilon>0
one nonzero-edge and one linearly vanishing-edge witness
seven bounded high-precision scalar quadratures with no roots or ODEs
not_computed: a quantum operator, ordering, self-adjoint domain, rigging map, or physical inner product for undensitized raw C
unitary equivalence between raw C, densitized H, or the declared Mc representation
a canonical p=0 endpoint counterterm, renormalization condition, origin-supported sector, or superselection rule
the p<0 component, both-branch completion, global chart, or self-adjoint relational Phi observable
a lapse contour or modulus, zero-lapse contact terms, full BFV trajectory measure, determinants, anomalies, or BRST cohomology
inhomogeneous metric modes, the local GR constraint algebra, gravitons, renormalization, observables, empirical predictions, quantum gravity, physics, or TOE
